seo.title: Best Libraries for Supabase in 2026
seo.description: Curated Supabase libraries for auth, file storage, real-time features, edge functions, and admin tooling. From real production usage.

introduction: Supabase gives you Postgres, auth, storage, and real-time out of the box — but the real power comes from the ecosystem built around it. I've used Supabase in three production apps and these libraries turned it from a nice backend into a full platform. Here's what actually works beyond the quickstart tutorial.

categories.name: Client Libraries & SDKs
categories.description: Official and community SDKs for integrating Supabase with different frameworks and languages.

items.name: supabase-js
items.description: The official JavaScript/TypeScript client. Handles auth, database queries, storage, and real-time subscriptions. Type-safe when paired with generated types. The starting point for any web project.
items.highlight: Full-featured client with type-safe database queries

items.name: @supabase/ssr
items.description: Server-side rendering helpers for Next.js, SvelteKit, and Remix. Handles cookie-based auth sessions correctly across server and client. Replaces the old auth-helpers packages.
items.highlight: Cookie-based auth that works correctly with SSR frameworks

items.name: supabase-flutter
items.description: Official Flutter SDK with support for all Supabase features. If you're building a cross-platform mobile app with a Supabase backend, this is well-maintained and keeps parity with supabase-js.
items.highlight: Full feature parity with supabase-js for cross-platform mobile

items.name: supabase-swift
items.description: Official Swift client for iOS and macOS apps. Covers auth, database, storage, and real-time. The API mirrors supabase-js closely, so knowledge transfers between platforms.

items.name: supabase-kt
items.description: Community Kotlin Multiplatform client for Android, iOS, and JVM. Covers core Supabase features with Kotlin coroutines. Solid alternative if your mobile team is Kotlin-first.

items.name: Supabase CLI
items.description: Local development, database migrations, type generation, and Edge Function deployment. The CLI is essential — run supabase gen types to get TypeScript types from your database schema.
items.highlight: Generate TypeScript types directly from your database schema

categories.name: Auth & Security
categories.description: Libraries that extend Supabase's authentication system with additional providers, access patterns, and security features.

items.name: Supabase Auth UI
items.description: Pre-built auth components for React and other frameworks. Drop in a login form with social providers, magic links, and email/password in one component. Customizable with Tailwind or custom CSS.
items.highlight: Complete auth UI in one component — social, magic link, email

items.name: Supabase Auth (Built-in)
items.description: Supabase's built-in auth system supports 20+ OAuth providers, magic links, phone auth, and email/password. Row Level Security integrates auth directly with database permissions. Powerful and free.
items.highlight: 20+ OAuth providers with RLS-integrated database permissions

items.name: Supabase Vault
items.description: Encrypted secrets storage built into Supabase. Store API keys, tokens, and sensitive configuration encrypted at rest in Postgres. Access from Edge Functions or server-side code.

items.name: pg_graphql
items.description: Supabase's Postgres extension that exposes your database as a GraphQL API automatically. Schema reflects your tables, RLS policies apply, and it runs at the database level for maximum performance.
items.highlight: Auto-generated GraphQL API from your Postgres schema

items.name: supabase-auth-helpers (Legacy)
items.description: The older framework-specific auth helpers for Next.js, SvelteKit, and Remix. Being replaced by @supabase/ssr but still used in many existing projects. Migrate when you can.

categories.name: Database & ORM
categories.description: Libraries for working with Supabase's Postgres database — ORMs, query builders, and migration tools.

items.name: Drizzle ORM
items.description: A TypeScript ORM that works beautifully with Supabase Postgres. SQL-like syntax with full type inference. Use drizzle-kit for migrations alongside Supabase's migration system.
items.highlight: Type-safe SQL queries that feel natural with Supabase

items.name: Prisma
items.description: The most popular TypeScript ORM works with Supabase Postgres out of the box. The Prisma schema is a great way to model your data, though you lose some Supabase-specific features like RLS integration.

items.name: Kysely
items.description: A type-safe SQL query builder that generates Supabase-compatible queries. More low-level than Drizzle or Prisma — you write SQL, but with TypeScript autocompletion and type checking.

items.name: pgvector
items.description: Supabase's vector similarity search extension for building AI features. Store embeddings alongside your data and query by similarity. Powers RAG applications, semantic search, and recommendations.
items.highlight: Vector similarity search for AI features — built into Postgres

items.name: PostgREST
items.description: The engine behind Supabase's auto-generated REST API. Turns your Postgres tables into RESTful endpoints with filtering, pagination, and RLS enforcement. Understanding PostgREST helps you master Supabase's API layer.

items.name: Supabase Migrations
items.description: Supabase's built-in migration system via the CLI. Write SQL migrations, version them in git, and apply them across environments. Simple and database-native — no ORM abstraction layer.

categories.name: Real-time & Edge Functions
categories.description: Libraries and tools for Supabase's real-time features, Edge Functions, and serverless capabilities.

items.name: Supabase Realtime
items.description: Built-in real-time engine that broadcasts database changes, presence information, and custom events over WebSockets. Subscribe to row-level changes with RLS enforcement. No additional server needed.
items.highlight: Real-time database changes over WebSockets with RLS

items.name: Supabase Edge Functions
items.description: Deno-based serverless functions deployed globally on Supabase's infrastructure. Handle webhooks, run background tasks, and build APIs close to your database. Cold starts are fast and deployment is instant.
items.highlight: Deno functions deployed globally — instant deployment

items.name: Supabase Cron (pg_cron)
items.description: Schedule recurring database tasks directly in Postgres. Run cleanup jobs, send reminders, aggregate analytics — all without an external scheduler. Cron expressions, database-native.

items.name: Supabase Queues (pgmq)
items.description: Message queues built into Postgres via the pgmq extension. Reliable job processing without Redis or RabbitMQ. Process tasks asynchronously from Edge Functions or external workers.
items.highlight: Message queues in Postgres — no Redis needed

items.name: Supabase Storage
items.description: S3-compatible file storage with automatic image transformations, resumable uploads, and RLS policies. Upload directly from the client with signed URLs. Handles avatars, documents, and media files.
items.highlight: S3-compatible storage with built-in image transformations

items.name: Supabase Webhooks
items.description: Trigger HTTP webhooks on database events — inserts, updates, and deletes. Call external APIs, send notifications, or sync data without polling. Configure via the dashboard or SQL.

categories.name: Admin & Tooling
categories.description: Tools for managing, monitoring, and administering Supabase projects in development and production.

items.name: Supabase Studio
items.description: The built-in database admin UI with a table editor, SQL editor, and visual schema designer. Surprisingly powerful for an included tool. Most tasks that require pgAdmin can be done here instead.
items.highlight: Full database admin UI included — rarely need pgAdmin

items.name: Supabase Local Development
items.description: Run the full Supabase stack locally with Docker via supabase start. Auth, database, storage, and Edge Functions all running on your machine. Test everything before pushing to production.
items.highlight: Full Supabase stack running locally via Docker

items.name: Supabase Branching
items.description: Preview branches that create isolated Supabase environments for each git branch. Test database changes and migrations in isolation before merging. Like Vercel preview deployments but for your backend.
items.highlight: Isolated backend environments per git branch

items.name: Supabase MCP
items.description: Model Context Protocol server for Supabase that lets AI assistants interact with your database, run queries, and manage resources. Connect Claude or other AI tools directly to your Supabase project.

items.name: dbdev (Database.dev)
items.description: A package manager for Postgres extensions hosted by Supabase. Install community extensions like pgvector, pg_graphql, and others directly into your Supabase project with a single command.

items.name: Supavisor
items.description: Supabase's Postgres connection pooler built in Elixir. Handles thousands of concurrent connections without overwhelming your database. Transparent to your app — just change the connection string.
